page: Amazon Web Services m7g.large is a general-purpose server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processors utilizing the ARM64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at 2.6 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, has a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1532.88 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1444.0. However, multi-core and multi-threaded scaling is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3040.69 and a poor bzip3 multi-threaded decompression result of 16.5 GB/sec. Memory performance is mixed; while large block read-only bandwidth is average at 53.4 GB/sec, small block cached reads and large block writes fall into the weak category.

The m7g.large offers a cost-efficient entry point into the Graviton7 ARM ecosystem, delivering dedicated compute resources and balanced memory density without the overhead of hyperthreading. Tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage and limited multi-threaded scaling. This profile makes the instance appropriate for general-purpose workloads such as light web serving, basic text processing, single-threaded application tasks, and development environments that do not require high multi-core throughput or local disk performance.
